title: Make a PDF Watermark Readable in Grayscale
description: Make a PDF text watermark easier to read in grayscale. Check one printed page and adjust color, size or opacity without hiding the document text.
direct: Try a neutral dark mark and proof one page in grayscale. Tune the weight until both the body and the mark read clearly.
figureAlt: Photo of an office proof page just outside a small grayscale printer
cards.decision.heading: Proof the page on paper
cards.decision.body: A vivid watermark color can become pale gray in print. Choose one page with a busy background or small text. The mark and the document both need to remain readable at a normal reading distance.
sections.detail-1.heading: Save the settings that worked
sections.detail-1.body: Record the watermark text, color and opacity for the other copies in the same set. Check any page with a different background before printing the full run.
sections.detail-2.heading: About the app
sections.detail-2.body: Space Sheep Studio develops this iPhone app. Check the App Store listing for current access and export options.
faqs.first-question.heading: What if nothing prints?
faqs.first-question.body: Reopen the exported file, check print preview and try another PDF viewer if the mark appears only on screen.
faqs.second-question.heading: Will the mark survive a photocopy?
faqs.second-question.body: That depends on the printer and copier settings. Proof an actual photocopy if you need that result.

steps.step-1.text: Open the source in PDF Watermark & Stamp. Try neutral dark text and preview the page that has the most detail.
steps.step-2.text: Export a test copy and print that page in grayscale on the printer and paper you plan to use.
steps.step-3.text: Adjust one setting at a time. Darken or enlarge a faint mark. Lower opacity or try a centered stamp if it competes with the body text.
